cases.evidence: The three inline test modules are replaced by path modules whose new files contain the same imports, test names, assertions, and values.
Stable custody and ingest contracts are revised to authorize same-ID recovery, fencing, cursor convergence, and restored-reading handling.
Bootstrap and broker-certificate validation now require an exact OpenSSL hostname-match message in addition to its exit status, changing certificate acceptance.
New stable recovery runbooks prescribe fencing, encrypted restore, no-backup loss acceptance, cursor convergence, and incident closure steps.
Every hunk only reflows existing Rust expressions or reorders adjacent re-exports without changing identifiers, calls, values, or assertions.
ACK handling now accepts stale duplicates and strict prior-prefix acknowledgements, and may advance only part of the current batch cursor.
The workspace package version and many Cargo.lock package entries change from 0.3.0 to 0.4.0, altering lockfile and build inputs.
A migration runner and baseline SQL create and persist _schema_version state, apply transactional migrations, and reject ahead schemas.
A configuration-mismatch error now directs operators to a specific reset command carrying an explicit trial-data-loss confirmation flag.
The v1 JSON wire field gateway_identity is renamed to edge_node_id in Rust, Go, fixtures, validation, and publication IDs; legacy-only payloads are rejected.
New source and bundled console output add five-second polling, request cancellation, live charts, stale status, and visible dashboard messages.
The console's visible sensor-details link changes from /sensors/{signal} to a device-scoped equipment route.
The test assertion changes from updated > first to updated > 100, but the supplied hunk does not establish that these predicates are equivalent.
The inline MQTT packet-limit test is moved verbatim to the path-selected unit-test file with the same import, setup, and assertion.
The sole change joins a method-chain expression onto one line while preserving the exact call sequence and operands.
Signal registration moves earlier, SIGTERM is added, cleanup and runtime shutdown gain deadlines, and cleanup timeout now forces a nonzero exit.
Three cfg(test) modules are replaced by path declarations, and the removed test bodies reappear verbatim in the referenced files; no production logic changes.
Stable EN/JA contracts are revised to authorize same-ID hardware recovery and define credential fencing, recovery authority, cursor convergence, and backup closure requirements.
Deployment and certificate-management scripts replace OpenSSL exit-status acceptance with an exact hostname-match output check, changing TLS certificate validation behavior.
New stable EN/JA recovery runbooks prescribe credential fencing, authenticated backup restore, loss-boundary approval, cursor convergence, and post-recovery backup requirements.
The diff only reflows expressions and import/export lists without changing identifiers, values, calls, assertions, or control flow.
ACK handling now accepts stale duplicates and prior-prefix acknowledgements and may advance only part of a batch, changing wire validation and durable cursor advancement semantics.
The workspace and lockfile package versions move from 0.3.0 to 0.4.0, while changelog and README release/version output are updated.
A production migration runner and baseline SQL create and mutate the persisted _schema_version table, apply transactional migrations, and reject schemas ahead of the binary.
The trial configuration error changes from a generic reset instruction to a concrete destructive reset command and recovery workflow shown to operators.
Serialized schema fields change from gateway_identity to edge_node_id, publication IDs change accordingly, and legacy payloads are explicitly rejected across Rust, Go, and fixtures.
A new polling live dashboard renders charts, values, freshness statuses, and failure summaries, with matching compiled console.js changes alongside the TypeScript source.
The rendered detail link changes from /sensors/{signal} to a device-scoped endpoint, altering operator navigation and the externally addressed route.
A test assertion changes from updated > first to updated > 100; the supplied hunk does not establish that first is always 100 or that the assertions are equivalent.
The cfg(test) module becomes a path declaration and its sole test body is reproduced verbatim in that referenced file; production MQTT code is unchanged.
Only line wrapping changes around the same host_str().is_some_and(host_is_loopback_ip) expression.
Signal registration moves earlier, SIGTERM support and shutdown deadlines are added, runtime teardown becomes bounded, and cleanup timeout now forces a nonzero exit.
Three cfg(test) modules move to path-addressed files with their test bodies unchanged; production code is untouched.
Stable custody and ingest contracts are revised to authorize encrypted-backup recovery, credential fencing, cursor convergence, and reactivation behavior.
Certificate hostname acceptance in bootstrap and broker-certificate workflows now requires an exact OpenSSL success message as well as a zero status.
New stable runbooks define backup and no-backup recovery paths, fencing gates, restored-data boundaries, and explicitly accepted loss boundaries.
The diff only reflows existing Rust expressions and import ordering without changing tokens that affect behavior.
ACK handling newly accepts stale and strict-prefix acknowledgements and can advance only part of the durable cursor, changing ordering and wire-acceptance semantics.
Workspace and lockfile package versions change from 0.3.0 to 0.4.0, while README and changelog expose the new release status.
The diff adds a schema-version table, migration SQL, transactional migration execution, and schema-ahead rejection.
A configuration-mismatch diagnostic now directs operators to a specific reset command that explicitly confirms trial data loss.
The v1 JSON field changes from gateway_identity to edge_node_id in Rust, Go, publication IDs, and fixtures, and legacy-only payloads are rejected.
A new live-dashboard source module and its bundled console.js output add polling, charts, values, and visible stale/never-received statuses.
The console's visible sensor-detail link changes from /sensors/... to an equipment/device-scoped destination.
The assertion changes from comparing updated against first to comparing it against 100; the diff does not establish those predicates are equivalent.
The cfg(test) MQTT packet-limit test moves verbatim to a path-addressed unit-test file; runtime code is unchanged.
A single method chain is reflowed onto one line with the expression unchanged.
Signal registration moves before startup work, SIGTERM is added, cleanup and runtime teardown gain deadlines, and timeout now forces a nonzero exit.
